pr_title: Bluetooth: host: Fix ATT indication deadlock in RX thread
pr_body:
Fix deadlock in RX thread when ATT all buffers are taken by ATT requests and the RX thread blocks waiting for an buffer.
Solve this by not having a reference to the ATT request buffer until the ATT response is received, instead get a new ATT buffer in the case where it has to be resent.

Fixes: #28685

Fix ATT transaction violation in indications if the application has not set a callback function. In this case the indication was not treated as a transaction, leading to transaction violation.

Fix security elevation not working properly when the elevation is done in a two-step, this can happen when MITM is not enforced and security level 3 is required on the attribute.

Fix SMP debug keys overwrite handling not allowing to overwrite debug keys with debug keys, and allowing debug keys to overwrite existing bond information.

@Vudentz we'd like to try and get this in for 2.5, please take a look.

@Vudentz I have put back the use of net_buf_append_bytes.

I also found another issue where the buf for the ATT request was not always freed.
On master branch this can be seen when the buffer is successfully allocated, but the storage for the ATT request is not successful and returns error. In this case an error code is returned without the buffer being freed.

In order to fix this issue I put released of the ATT request buffer into the `bt_att_req_free` function, and eliminated the ATT internal `att_req_destroy` function.

The changes since last view can bee looked at here:
https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/compare/3b4b9c62882a3eb72d4972e822b9b0c9a0a2c571..329c2e9358ae77c0ff301c8305364e1c1d6f7ede

Regarding the use of net_buf_append_bytes, I still don't understand why this should be there, and I think maybe you misunderstood what I said?
The size of the buf is determined by our L2CAP TX MTU, you said "no it is not allocated according to the remote MTU".
I'm sure that the condition write != len will never happen because we check this before we allocate the buffer, and either allocate a write-request, or a prepare-write-req with the L2CAP TX MTU.

issue_context.title: Bluetooth: Characteristic unsubscribe under indication load results in ATT timeout
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**

Conditions:
* Zephyr device acting as a GATT server
* Many indications are being generated in a loop in response to an event (accelerometer)
* GATT client attempts to unsubscribe from the indication characteristic while indications are queued

This sequence reliably results in an ATT timeout, normally due to a failure to allocate a buffer for the "write response" to the CCC write. The unsubscribe request in the below log is sent at ~00:02:07.
```
00> [00:02:03.931,365] <wrn> uc_bt_gatt: DATA: Subscribed 2
00> [00:02:37.906,616] <wrn> bt_conn: Unable to allocate buffer within timeout
00> [00:02:37.906,646] <err> bt_att: Unable to allocate buffer for op 0x13, 0
00> [00:02:37.919,097] <err> bt_att: ATT Timeout
00> [00:02:37.919,128] <wrn> uc_bt_gatt: DATA: Indication failed 14
00> [00:02:37.919,158] <wrn> uc_bt_gatt: DATA: Indication failed 14
00> [00:02:37.919,158] <wrn> uc_bt_gatt: DATA: Indication failed 14
00> [00:02:37.919,219] <wrn> uc_bt_gatt: DATA: Subscribed 0
00> [00:02:37.919,250] <err> bt_conn: not connected!
00> [00:02:37.919,281] <wrn> bt_att: No pending ATT request
00> [00:02:37.919,372] <err> bt_gatt: Error sending ATT PDU: -128
```

On the server, indications are broadcast normally to anyone that has subscribed through:
```
for (int i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    indicate_params.attr = &uc_svc.attrs[DATA_ATTR_INDEX];
    indicate_params.data = message->data;
    indicate_params.len = message->len;
    indicate_params.func = uc_bt_data_indicate_cb;
    bt_gatt_indicate(NULL, &indicate_params);
}
```
With the `uc_bt_data_indicate_cb` printing the errors from the above log
```
if (err) {
	LOG_WRN("DATA: Indication failed %d", err);
}
```

Presumably all available TX buffers have been claimed by the indication loop, leaving no buffers for the write response.

Probably relevant Kconfig symbols
```
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_RX_BUFFERS 6
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_TX_BUFFERS 3
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_TX_BUFFER_SIZE 251
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_TX_PWR_PLUS_8 1
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_LE_ENC 1
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_CONN_PARAM_REQ 1
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_EXT_REJ_IND 1
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_SLAVE_FEAT_REQ 1
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_LE_PING 1
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_PRIVACY 1
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_RL_SIZE 8
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_EXT_SCAN_FP 1
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_DATA_LENGTH 1
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_DATA_LENGTH_MAX 251
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_MIN_USED_CHAN 1
#define CONFIG_BT_CTLR_CHAN_SEL_2 1
#define CONFIG_BT_HCI_CMD_COUNT 2
#define CONFIG_BT_RX_BUF_COUNT 3
#define CONFIG_BT_RX_BUF_LEN 76
#define CONFIG_BT_CONN_TX_MAX 3
#define CONFIG_BT_AUTO_DATA_LEN_UPDATE 1
#define CONFIG_BT_L2CAP_RX_MTU 252
#define CONFIG_BT_L2CAP_TX_BUF_COUNT 3
#define CONFIG_BT_L2CAP_TX_FRAG_COUNT 2
#define CONFIG_BT_L2CAP_TX_MTU 252
#define CONFIG_BT_ATT_ENFORCE_FLOW 1
#define CONFIG_BT_ATT_PREPARE_COUNT 0
#define CONFIG_BT_ATT_TX_MAX 3
```

**Expected behavior**
Server should respond with an acknowledgement to the CCC write, and any pending indications should be dropped.

While this is caused by insufficient `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_TX_BUFFERS`, it should be possible for the controller to iterate over queued packets on a characteristic if it is being unsubscribed from and dequeue them before trying to allocate the write response packet.

**Impact**
Annoyance, normally we don't unsubscribe until we are done with a connection.
While the connection is unusable after an ATT Timeout, reconnecting fixes the issue.

Increasing `CONFIG_BT_CTLR_TX_BUFFERS` from the default value also reduces the chances of the TX buffer starvation.

**Logs and console output**

Wireshark Capture of the server failing to respond (unacknowledged write is packet 1127)
[IndicateUnsub.zip](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/files/5280073/IndicateUnsub.zip)

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - Zephyr 2.4-rc3


**Workaround:**
Make sure that ATT requests cannot acquire all the buffers in the system setting CONFIG_BT_L2CAP_TX_BUF_COUNT  >= CONFIG_BT_ATT_TX_MAX + 2

> @Vudentz any input on this one?

Indication do require a response so the are not queued in the controller, instead we queue them the host and wait the other requests to complete.

There might be some problem with BT_ATT_TX_MAX though. if we can queue all buffers then we are likely to create such problems since one can exaust the buffer pool on TX alone the response also fail waiting for a free buffer, we could attempt to dequeue and free the buffer but I wonder if it wouldn't be a better idea to not use the same pool for requests and response, that way we can garantee responses do not have to wait for a buffer that is allocate for a request which has a much longer lifetime when queued.

review_comments:
SMP_FLAG_KEYS_DISTR is set from bt_smp_encrypt_change() so this depends on order of registering channels

since channels are registered via BT_L2CAP_CHANNEL_DEFINE macro order seems to depend on linker action

I looked into the finished `zephyr.elf` and this is the order.
```
<att_fixed_chan>:
 <le_fixed_chan>:
<smp_fixed_chan>:
```
I'm pretty sure that the order is alphabetical, because the we seem to rely on this behavior for the static GATT service declararions, e.g:
```
<_1_gatt_svc>:
<_2_gap_svc>:
```

The request for a higher security level is not done immediately in the att_encrypt_change handler, instead the att_encrypt_change handler retransmits the ATT request that trigger security escalation. And then on a new ATT error PDU with error indication higher security level required do we request the next security level. But this is happening before the key distribution is finished.

That being said I'm fine with taking this particular fix out and fixing it separately, because I'm fairly confident we have  other cases where this would fail, for example ATT and L2CAP both initiating security at the same time, or with EATT on multiple enhanced ATT bearers at the same time.

This bug was only reproducible if both devices have the BT_SMP_ENFORCE_MITM option disabled (or the peer is acting in a similar way). This option is default on.
We might be better off chaning bt_att_req_alloc to take all these parameters intead of having a wrapper on gatt.c that just initializes the structure.

The reason why that wasn't possible at the moment was the bt_gatt_indicate. In order to make indications fit we will have to add a stack internal variable in the indication params to hold the resolved handle, since finding the handle is a rather complicated piece of code and should be kept out of the encode function IMO.
